reviews.title: Works but beware
reviews.text: I loved this app it works well and I was happy to pat for the upgraded plan. Then they charged me twice in 24 hours when I signed up. I should have known there were going to be problems when I looked up how to request a refund for the one I clearly could not use and found you can not. There policy is “Sorry for the inconvenience. Double charging can happen if you buy a Web subscription before your App Store/Google Play subscription expires-there's no refund or prorated credit in that case. To avoid this, cancel in Apple/Google and wait for expiration, then purchase via Web. You can also review receipts in your Otter account billing/payment history.” Problem is I didn’t sign up twice so I disputed with my card and moved on. Then I was in a meeting and even though all notifications are turned off and I checked every setting it set a notice that I hit the 30 minute limit which is what happens of the free plans but not the paid as you get 90 minute meetings. The biggest part of the frustration is the simple fact that I have every option for notifications turned off, and I do not share with the people with me in any capacity, this is for my own personal use. But the fact that the app just announced, it’s presence without any warning is extremely frustrating. These two things have made it so that the app that does work quite well and I do appreciate the AI integration being fairly flawless in being able to extract information such as action items and summaries is not worth potentia

reviews.title: Overcharging & Recording Without My Knowledge!
reviews.text:
I wasn't even aware that there were auto-recurring charges to my credit card resulting in hundreds of dollars of loss + credit card interest. I used it 2-3 times, and got charged for 1.5 years. 

Also, the app was recording my activities when it was installed and conferences online, some of them very confidential without my knowledge. I suspect that my data was also sold to online data brokers, which would explain the increase in targeted ads. It's also a security risk. What an invasion of privacy without my knowledge! And it wasn't installed for at least a year, yet I was charged for it nonetheless. It's borderline fraud.

reviews.title: Wow.  This is how former kings fall
reviews.text: Otter was the king of AI transcribing before ChatGPT was a thing.   The secret weapon.  Then like many lazy kings they do things at 50%.  Example: I had a dozen meetings last week so I paid the quite expensive monthly subscription cost. Now I need otter to do what every other AI platform can do today: go through each of those 12 meeting scripts and take notes for each meeting in the following ways:  then I take the time and give the AI about two paragraphs of specific requests.  Easy stuff like for each meeting use the contents to title the meeting in a more helpful way then the otter AI meeting titles. “Chuck” “Bob” should be “met with Bob to discuss sales trends over last two years”.  Ok? And I include mention like use subtitles for “person speaking” and put what they say under their name per each convo.  So what does dodo do? I mean otter.  It just puts “person name” thirty times throughout the notes.  Bro.  Really? ChatGPT 3.5 turbo was great but 2023 is the past homie.   Somebody at otter is pinching Pennies and thinking shortsighted when they should be claiming ground as king of kings using at least sonnet latest.   Not running a home made LLM on a Mac Studio cluster to save money. Because no way bro.  I am definitely finding a better transcription solution from here on out.  For 20 bucks or whatever  paid for this that’s a bad value these days and there’s even a limit to the number of minutes I have.  Fight over crumbs and you’ll be fighting over crumbs for sure in fiv

reviews.title: Transcription was accurate, ai summary was good, buuut
reviews.text:
It was nice to be able to get my thoughts out quickly and have the brainstorming session summarized. However this seems to be a tool designed for desktop users. The real deal breaker for me is the lack of practical usability for my needs. 

1)The inability to simply move a recording/session into a folder for categorization.  I clocked the ••• and selected move to folder. Nothing happens. Am i supposed to hold it? Or is there a drag and drop. 

2)the getting started instructions are for a desktop user layout. I feebly tried to use the self help and would have continued to try and work it out but when troubleshooting with the AI chat, if i went back into the app to attempt the suggestion, there was no way to get back to that chatbot again.  I had initially clicked on the popup “chat now/or whatever the chatbot link was” but i couldn’t get back to it. 

As a truck driver i cant be looking at screens and trying to troubleshoot things to learn how to use an expensive app. Need to be click and go.  

I will circle back around to this program again someday but im not interested in spending money to help a designer troubleshoot their own app. 

Thank you for your hard work and im sure this helps many many many people. Its a very cool tool.  It’s simply not practical for my needs.

reviews.title: Not what it used to be
reviews.text: When I first started using this app several years ago it literally changed my life. It worked great and quick and it was well priced. It still is very helpful. But it has become much more expensive! And it takes a LOT longer to get the job done. I had a 15 minute voice recording that I needed transcribed today at work. I quickly loaded it up thinking maybe 15-20 minutes would be really long. Then I waited….all afternoon! It was 3+ hours. The workday was long over before I could even get started. That never happened when the app was free…or then when it was $11/ mo…or then when it was $15/ mo. Now that it is more than $30/mo, it runs so slow that it makes me miss my deadlines. Not acceptable. Not sure what my solution is. But I guess I gotta go shopping again.
